kenney.label: Hanging slime, not approved mushroom art; excluded brazier

onebit.label: Hanging slime, not approved mushroom art; excluded brazier

cards.decisions: This is an exclusion record, not a request to reverse earlier decisions. Comment only if you deliberately want to revisit an exclusion.
cards.existing: Mushroom scenery, selected flasks/braziers and abandoned rails already exist. Hittable spore pods and bombs were rejected; moving carts were not selected.

groups.label: Hanging slime, not approved mushroom art; excluded brazier

cards.idea: Preserve the rejected flask/brazier variants and the hanging-slime reading. No spore-pod or bomb mechanic is proposed.
cards.title: Previously excluded art — keep on hold

cards.decisions: These remain visible for completeness. Comment if a particular cell has been misread; no unrelated vehicle/electronics feature is proposed.
cards.existing: Their presence in a general-purpose source sheet does not mean ROAG needs spaceships, trains or handheld consoles.
cards.idea: Keep overtly modern vehicle/electronic-looking motifs out of the current fantasy proposals.
cards.title: Modern/vehicle motifs — setting mismatch

cards.decisions: Needs corpse records, locked occupancy, cancellation and save tests. Revived units must not farm XP/gold. Hooded figures are candidates, not a named official necromancer.
cards.existing: Mend Acolytes heal living allies and Forge Conjurers summon; neither revives the dead.
cards.idea: A fragile caster commits one revival of a fallen ally. Occupy the marked corpse tile or kill the caster to stop it; the group has one revival budget.
cards.title: Grave Cantor + finite resurrection

cards.decisions: Choose its tell, wake action, reward and minimap treatment. Tiny #92 reads as an open mimic-like chest; 1-Bit can use a chest-to-ghost reveal.
cards.existing: Vault Lurkers ambush and vaults can spawn enemies. A container-to-enemy transition would be new.
cards.idea: A visibly suspicious chest wakes into a locked, telegraphed bite rather than granting an immediate free ambush hit.
cards.title: Haunted cache / chest mimic

cards.decisions: Define wall/occupied-cell collisions and stairs. Reject illegal landings and do not guarantee reaction time. A blocked shove must have a clear result.
cards.existing: Glass Charger moves itself; Hookrunner pulls AI enemies. Player displacement is not currently supported by the shared displacement operation.
cards.idea: A slow enemy locks a one-tile shove toward brambles, bog or a partner’s snare. Moving sideways or baiting the strike changes its landing.
cards.title: Heavy Rammer + positional shove

cards.decisions: Cap active webs, preserve an exit, show endpoints through fog correctly and save their remaining state. No real-time spreading or simulation on render.
cards.existing: Snare Scribe already places individual floor traps. Anchored, breakable lines supply a different route decision.
cards.idea: A spider commits a line between two visible anchors. Crossing consumes the web and adds recovery; destroying an anchor clears the line.
cards.title: Web Weaver + anchored webs

cards.decisions: No unseen spawn, occupied landing or floor transition. Attack and relocation must remain separate commitments.
cards.existing: Gloom Strider skirmishes and Shade has a decoy swap; this is an enemy relocation commitment, not hidden teleport damage.
cards.idea: A hollow figure marks its destination before phasing to a visible, legal tile. Standing on the destination cancels the move.
cards.title: Hollow Wraith + announced phase step

cards.decisions: No removal from player inventory and no duplicate rewards. Do not consume unique keys or make route completion depend on the toad.
cards.existing: Food/health/currency drops already exist. No enemy currently carries a specific swallowed pickup.
cards.idea: A bulky creature visibly swallows one nearby loose drop, then carries it until defeated. The player can intercept it or fight for the same drop.
cards.title: Gulp Toad + recoverable stolen drop

cards.decisions: Must preview both paths, bound reflection to one bounce and preserve friendly fire. DOT/boon chains must not recursively reflect.
cards.existing: Shield Bearer blocks its front wedge. This proposal redirects a limited attack class rather than adding another all-purpose shield.
cards.idea: A caster marks one reflective lane. A later direct ranged attack through it reflects along a previewed cardinal path; side attacks and melee bypass it.
cards.title: Mirror Hexer + reflected lane

cards.decisions: Cap trail cells and lifetime in simulation time. Keep stairs/doors free and restore underlying terrain exactly after expiry.
cards.existing: Bog already increases recovery; Glass Charger already commits movement. The new decision is the visible trailing lane.
cards.idea: A worm announces a short charge and leaves two temporary bog cells behind it. The trail changes approach costs, not the whole floor.
cards.title: Silt Worm + temporary bog trail

cards.decisions: Needs simultaneous batch rules, no recursive secondary procs and fog-clipped links. Agree whether separation or one death breaks the oath permanently.
cards.existing: Ward Weaver prevents damage and healers restore it. A shared finite HP-loss link would be a different group puzzle.
cards.idea: Two enemies visibly share part of incoming damage while their short LOS link is intact. Separate them with geometry or displacement before committing an area attack.
cards.title: Oath Twins + breakable pain link

cards.decisions: Reinforcements must appear at marked legal cells, with fixed eligibility for rewards. A failed placement must not block the floor.
cards.existing: Captains buff existing followers; Conjurer summons repeatedly up to its cap. This keeper has one call and never creates an infinite stream.
cards.idea: A bell-bearing keeper commits a long visible alarm. Killing or stunning it cancels a single bounded reinforcement group.
cards.title: Alarm Keeper + one interruptible call

cards.decisions: Do not reinterpret rejected spore pods as this enemy. No hidden landing, guaranteed dodge or long-lived terrain flood.
cards.existing: Rushwings already flank; Burning already exists. The moth pressures space after its strike instead of healing or coordinating a pack.
cards.idea: A flying creature locks a landing cell and leaves a short-lived ember there after impact. The landing and follow-up hazard remain visibly distinct.
cards.title: Ember Moth + readable burning landing

cards.decisions: One total reward budget, capped fragments, legal occupied-cell handling and saved split state. Do not prolong every ordinary fight.
cards.existing: Existing enemies summon or revive no such death fragments. The primary death HP batch must still finish before secondary spawns.
cards.idea: A skeleton collapses into two weak fragments after its first defeat. Destroy the fragments to finish the encounter; they cannot split again.
cards.title: Bone Splitter + reward-bounded fragments

cards.decisions: Keep every footprint locked; stop the sequence on stun/death/displacement. Decide whether it is a room champion or a future miniboss.
cards.existing: Shield Bearer and existing bosses already have facing/phase rules. This is a potential encounter, not another permanent invulnerable front.
cards.idea: An optional armoured champion commits successive quarter-turn strikes. Its next facing is announced, creating a circular positioning puzzle.
cards.title: Rotating Sentinel encounter

cards.decisions: Not an exploding spore pod. Eggs are separate marked spawn targets, not damaging mystery scenery; cap enemies and rewards.
cards.existing: Forge Conjurer already summons, so anchor destruction and a finite budget must be the distinguishing decisions.
cards.idea: A creature marks two hatching anchors. Destroying an anchor cancels its one hatch; the keeper cannot replenish them.
cards.title: Brood Keeper + finite hatching anchors

cards.decisions: Only two vetted shapes, fixed stats and normal locked timing. Display its chosen shape before resolution; never steal or disable a player boon.
cards.existing: Temporal Echo is a boon and several enemies use sweeps. This enemy reads a small recorded action category rather than copying arbitrary boon code.
cards.idea: A duelist shows whether its next committed strike copies a short line or a sweep from the player’s last eligible attack.
cards.title: Echo Duelist + copied attack shape

cards.decisions: No free guaranteed reaction action. Define which direct attacks can be parried and make the window use scheduler time.
cards.existing: Adventurer is balanced, Berserker cleaves, Sentinel is defensive and Hookrunner pulls. The new decision is timing one paid defensive commitment.
cards.idea: A light blade class uses a narrow thrust, a committed parry window and a sidestep. A successful parry funds one riposte instead of granting passive invulnerability.
cards.title: Duelist — precision and paid riposte

cards.decisions: Never seal required access, stairs or an occupied tile. Store original terrain and a simulation-time expiry; published art must not own collision.
cards.existing: Arcanist attacks zones, Trapper lays snares. A deliberately placed temporary LOS/movement obstacle is a different role.
cards.idea: A caster raises one short-lived stone block on an adjacent legal cell, shaping a firing lane before a heavy stone strike.
cards.title: Geomancer — one temporary bulwark

cards.decisions: Needs friendly ownership, cap, save state and reward rules. Never use render dt or allow a familiar to scout unseen rooms for free.
cards.existing: Shade’s decoy draws attacks and swaps once. This spirit performs bounded damage under explicit orders rather than autonomous free attacks.
cards.idea: Command one bound spirit to occupy a visible nearby cell or attack a locked target. Repositioning it costs the player an ordinary action.
cards.title: Spiritbinder — one commanded familiar

cards.decisions: No permanent meta advantage, healing exploit or accidental lethal toggle. Preview the exact cost and the one-action benefit.
cards.existing: Berserker is durable/high damage and Alchemist throws flasks. This is an explicit finite HP expenditure, not free regeneration.
cards.idea: A close-range pilgrim trades a clearly shown amount of current HP for one empowered action, then returns to ordinary attacks.
cards.title: Pilgrim — spend health for a measured vow

cards.decisions: Needs friendly-fire, target visibility, ownership, occupancy and save rules. No wall penetration, automatic scouting or unlimited wait farming.
cards.existing: Ranger shoots directly and Trapper controls movement. A finite deployed attacker adds setup and line-of-fire decisions.
cards.idea: Place one visible bolt sentry with three charges. Each shot follows an explicitly scheduled commitment; replacing it discards remaining charges.
cards.title: Tinkerer — one limited bolt sentry

cards.decisions: No extra boon proc coefficient loophole. Decide whether this is distinct enough to justify a class before implementing it.
cards.existing: Arcanist already has lightning and fire zones; the distinction must be a capped choice between expenditure modes, not a recolour.
cards.idea: Build a small visible charge through direct hits, spend it on a delayed locked cross, or ground it into a one-hit ward.
cards.title: Stormcaller — charge, ground, discharge

cards.decisions: Reject walls, occupied landings, doors and stairs as necessary. Approve only if the difference from Shade is useful enough.
cards.existing: Shade already swaps with a decoy. The beacon does not draw attacks; it offers deliberate retreat and cannot scout or cross floors.
cards.idea: Plant one beacon on explored ground, then spend the movement ability to return within a bounded same-room distance.
cards.title: Wayfinder — a visible return beacon

cards.decisions: No real-time beat test and no party-wide free buff. Requires a simple saved capped phrase and clearly previewed payoff.
cards.existing: There is no rhythm minigame or animation timeline. World time still advances only through ordinary legal actions.
cards.idea: Alternate thrust and pulse to build a displayed three-note phrase, then spend it on a local push or direct hit.
cards.title: Cantor — a three-note attack phrase

cards.decisions: Agree the cost, lethal-use policy, confirmation and one-use save state. Do not require payment to complete the route.
cards.existing: Shrine room templates and gold chests exist, but no HP-payment altar interaction does.
cards.idea: Choose a boon offer in exchange for an explicit HP payment at an optional font.
cards.title: One-use HP offering font

cards.decisions: One use, no explosive barrel, no extra break-for-gold duplicate. Reward quantities need pacing tests.
cards.existing: Food/health drops and a three-action ward already exist. This combines existing effects in one explicit choice, not a new hunger system.
cards.idea: A finite cache offers immediate food or a short ward, letting the player choose recovery versus the next fight.
cards.title: Sealed ration cache

cards.decisions: Decide immediate-use versus one carried charge. Do not introduce a full inventory UI for one potion.
cards.existing: Burning and healing exist; no poison system is assumed.
cards.idea: A clearly labelled dose removes Burning now instead of healing HP. It can be selected from an optional supply choice.
cards.title: Single-use cleansing flask

cards.decisions: Choose charge storage, pickup behavior and LOS/wall rules. No unseen teleport or stair activation through the scroll.
cards.existing: Dash already exists. A carried consumable would be new and must not replace class identity.
cards.idea: Spend a finite charge to step to a previewed visible legal cell at short range; the move consumes a committed action.
cards.title: One-charge escape scroll

cards.decisions: Only if a carried-charge workflow is approved. No return across floors, occupied cells or closed gates.
cards.existing: Would share landing validation with the proposed Wayfinder, without giving every class a permanent teleport.
cards.idea: A one-use token returns the player to a deliberately placed, same-room marker when a normal action is spent.
cards.title: Room-bound return token

cards.decisions: Use explicit action counts and finite use. Agree on the alternatives and reward pacing before adding numbers.
cards.existing: Ward flask already exists. The new choice must be a small mutually exclusive menu rather than automatic buffs.
cards.idea: A well offers one clearly stated temporary condition, such as a ward for the next three committed actions, instead of another permanent boon.
cards.title: Charm well — choose one short condition

cards.decisions: Decide title-only practice versus an explicitly separate practice fixture. Training must be achievement-ineligible and never alter a saved run.
cards.existing: Nine classes already exist. This is an onboarding/training room, not unrequested collectible weapons.
cards.idea: A safe optional rack previews existing class attacks on inert targets without changing the current run’s class or consuming gameplay rewards.
cards.title: Practice rack — preview before choosing

cards.decisions: Must preserve frozen run pool, rarity accounting, deterministic offers, transformations and cancellation. Agree exact trade rules first.
cards.existing: Current chests give three offers and mixed-rarity stacks are uncapped. This adds a controlled build correction, not a free rarity upgrade.
cards.idea: At a one-use forge, explicitly trade one selected boon stack and gold for one previewed alternative offer.
cards.title: Attunement forge — trade one stack

cards.decisions: No resale loop, inventory overhaul or refresh-farming. Fix stock and prices in the floor snapshot.
cards.existing: Gold chests already supply boons. The trader needs a useful service choice rather than cheaper duplicate rewards.
cards.idea: An optional stall offers two finite services, such as food versus an already-generated boon offer, at visible gold prices.
cards.title: One-visit supply trader

cards.decisions: Approve only if losing a boon feels worthwhile. Needs transformation rollback, mixed-rarity stack selection and deterministic save continuation.
cards.existing: This is different from a free heal and from the proposed forge’s alternate offer.
cards.idea: An optional memorial trades one chosen stack for immediate recovery, with the exact effect previewed before confirmation.
cards.title: Memorial — retire a boon for recovery

cards.decisions: At most one bounce per reflector and bounded traversal. No arbitrary ray engine, moving bullet requirement or mandatory puzzle gate.
cards.existing: Keys and timed plates exist. This is a spatial relay rather than another plate timer.
cards.idea: Reorient a small fixed set of reflectors to route a visible beam into a receiver, opening an optional cache.
cards.title: Mirror relay room

cards.decisions: Reset behavior and readable symbols must be clear. Audio may reinforce the clue but must not be required.
cards.existing: Sidequests already record clues/plate state. This adds a short visible sequence, not real-time rhythm input.
cards.idea: Read three pictorial clues and activate stationary bells in that order for an optional reward.
cards.title: Bell-order side room

cards.decisions: Colours need distinct shapes in 1-Bit. Keep sockets/frames separate from traversable ground and cap state combinations.
cards.existing: Crystal terrain reacts to lightning already. This is a room objective and should reuse that rule where possible.
cards.idea: Activate fixed coloured sockets to connect a short displayed relay. A wrong choice resets the relay without unavoidable damage.
cards.title: Prism socket relay

cards.decisions: Never activate from render dt, place unavoidable spawn damage or hide the warning under fog. Needs saved phase and next due time.
cards.existing: Burning exists; static decorative hearths are not hazards by default.
cards.idea: A small vent alternates warning, impact and cooldown at explicit simulation timestamps. It pressures a route without relying on animation speed.
cards.title: Clocked heat vents

cards.decisions: Both states need connectivity checks. Never flood an occupied cell, required stairs or the only route; no full fluid system.
cards.existing: Water is static movement-blocking terrain. This is a saved discrete switch, not liquid simulation.
cards.idea: One visible lever changes a bounded set of water cells between two authored states, revealing an optional crossing.
cards.title: Two-state sluice room

cards.decisions: Depends on safe player displacement. Bound chains, resolve blocked landings and keep mandatory exits safe.
cards.existing: This is a discrete terrain effect, not a moving train/cart or physical conveyor simulation.
cards.idea: Arrow-marked cells add one legal-tile push after entry. The strip can be used tactically by both sides.
cards.title: Push-floor strip

cards.decisions: Prove alternate routes before placement, restore/save its exact state and forbid occupied-cell collapse damage.
cards.existing: Barricades break and timed gates close already. This would be a one-way optional shortcut, not a required collapsing floor.
cards.idea: A cracked bridge segment clearly warns that it will close after one crossing, giving a shortcut with an alternate return route.
cards.title: Fragile optional crossing

cards.decisions: Visible trigger and delay, one saved use, and no hidden enemy tracking after commitment. Must not obstruct mandatory routes.
cards.existing: Not a volatile bomb or spore pod. It is an explicit one-use room trap with friendly fire.
cards.idea: A suspended fixture can be triggered from a marked switch; it first locks a small impact area, then falls through the normal scheduler.
cards.title: Announced falling fixture

cards.decisions: Only show information the sign is intended to disclose. Avoid misleading signs unless that is separately approved.
cards.existing: Route choices, fog and secrets already exist. This adds readable local hints, not full-map revelation.
cards.idea: A sign near a branch hints at an already-generated room’s reward or danger category, helping navigation without revealing its exact geometry.
cards.title: Pictorial route signposts

cards.decisions: No unlimited wait healing or normal-run reset. Decide whether a camp replaces a chest slot or adds a rarer side room.
cards.existing: Food and wards exist; this is a visible pacing node rather than another permanent stat bonus.
cards.idea: A tent offers one finite rest choice: recover now or prepare a short ward. Leaving commits the choice.
cards.title: One-use camp choice

cards.decisions: Never disable controls silently. Explicit failure/cancellation and no profile rewards from practice or developer fixtures.
cards.existing: Sidequests already exist. The new piece is a voluntarily accepted, visible action constraint.
cards.idea: Accept a clearly scoped room challenge, such as clearing its marked enemies without using Dash, for a fixed optional reward.
cards.title: Archivist’s optional contract

cards.decisions: Define exit/failure behavior before closing any gate. No weakened fixture should be claimed as an ordinary legal victory.
cards.existing: Elites and optional secrets exist. This is an opt-in teaching room, not a second boss progression.
cards.idea: Enter a clearly labelled short arena with one fixed enemy pattern to learn its counterplay, then take one fixed reward.
cards.title: Optional sparring trial

cards.decisions: Clues must remain visible without a specific colour pack. No new collision inferred from the image.
cards.existing: Crack and spiral clues already exist. This is a readability and art expansion, not another secret reward system.
cards.idea: Use spare face/sigil art as local clue variants for existing secret mechanisms.
cards.title: Readable secret murals

cards.decisions: Choose dressing-only versus full biome. Full biome needs signature mechanic, route/boss/generation/save acceptance. Never use grave props as floor.
cards.existing: Seven biomes and unique minibosses already exist. Art alone does not define a new biome.
cards.idea: A bone-and-grave environment could become an optional room family or a future eighth biome.
cards.title: Ossuary / crypt environment kit

cards.decisions: Review ground and wall parts separately; test every connected edge and corner in actual generated rooms.
cards.existing: Could enrich current rooms before adding a biome. The kit is not a ready-made connected terrain implementation.
cards.idea: Assemble pale stone floors, walls and columns for a readable sanctuary or crypt room family.
cards.title: Pale sanctuary — ground and masonry

kenney.label: Posts, fences and frame parts; no wood colour

onebit.label: Posts, fences and frame parts; no wood colour

cards.decisions: Supports stay on walls/props, never repeated as ground. A new timber palette needs a game-scale seam and readability review.
cards.existing: Abandoned rails and ore are already approved. This is a stronger environment kit for those rooms.

groups.label: Posts, fences and frame parts; no wood colour

cards.idea: Use wood surfaces and support assemblies to make mining rooms distinguishable without moving carts.
cards.title: Timber mine — floors, frames and braces

kenney.label: Geometric material samples; assemble, do not treat every sample as a full floor

onebit.label: Geometric material samples; assemble, do not treat every sample as a full floor

cards.decisions: Keep player/enemy/telegraph contrast and use full connected-wall composition tests.
cards.existing: The biome already exists. This is a palette/material improvement, not new icy movement rules.

groups.label: Geometric material samples; assemble, do not treat every sample as a full floor

cards.idea: Give Glacial Observatory a more precise pale/cool material set with matching carved accents.
cards.title: Observatory mosaic and cold stone

cards.decisions: Decoration must not imply blocking unless assigned as a real prop. Preserve approved mushroom art.
cards.existing: Trees and mushroom scenery already exist. No hittable spore-pod mechanic is being reopened.
cards.idea: Use grass, flowers, shrubs and tree variants to distinguish side gardens and current Ruins rooms.
cards.title: Root garden and overgrown courts

cards.decisions: Keep water/collision separate, check all corners, and use transparent water pieces over compatible bases only.
cards.existing: Water already blocks movement while permitting sight/projectiles. Art must not silently change that rule.
cards.idea: Assemble water boundaries, arches and submerged accents for Aqueduct rooms.
cards.title: Drowned sanctum water kit

kenney.label: Shared masonry and bars; monochrome counterpart

onebit.label: Shared masonry and bars; monochrome counterpart

cards.decisions: No unrelated industrial/space mechanics. Audit every multi-cell gate’s role and retain current navigation.
cards.existing: These biomes already have terrain and enemies; iron-looking art is not automatically an impassable block.

groups.label: Shared masonry and bars; monochrome counterpart

cards.idea: Strengthen Forge/Bastion identity with dark framing, iron gates and mechanical accents.
cards.title: Forge masonry and ironworks

cards.decisions: Carpet border pieces are ground decoration, not walls. Keep tactical overlays legible over coloured patterns.
cards.existing: Floor visuals currently convey biome identity through a small material set. This adds room-level variation.
cards.idea: Use coherent carpet borders to distinguish Archive chambers and safe reading alcoves.
cards.title: Archive carpets and patterned ground

cards.decisions: Do not paint doorway/gate images as floors. Review occlusion and fog boundaries at wall corners.
cards.existing: Generation already creates connected rooms; this changes appearance before considering any collision changes.
cards.idea: Add damaged wall silhouettes and nonblocking rubble dressing to make cave rooms less repetitive.
cards.title: Broken cavern — rubble, damaged edges, cave mouths

kenney.label: Shared masonry family, not a distinct new colour palette

onebit.label: Shared masonry family, not a distinct new colour palette

cards.decisions: Material families need connected 47-mask visual tests. Approval of a pool does not mean every fragment is a floor tile.
cards.existing: Current wall/water mask coverage is complete; spare cells add stylistic choices, not missing collision geometry.

groups.label: Shared masonry family, not a distinct new colour palette

cards.idea: Offer several coherent masonry families for the existing Ruins, with corners selected as a set.
cards.title: Ruins masonry variants

cards.decisions: Keep passable ground distinct from walls/props and verify patch seams at native scale.
cards.existing: This can remain inside the existing room generator; no outdoor world or new algorithm is required.
cards.idea: Ground-only variants and rounded borders for optional open courts and room transitions.
cards.title: Open-court grass and dirt ground

cards.decisions: Choose safe ground versus separately marked heat vents. Review colour contrast for hostile attacks.
cards.existing: Existing Burning is gameplay; orange pixels alone must not create damage.
cards.idea: A warm ground set could improve Sundered Forge or become a cosmetic room variant.
cards.title: Warm embers / fired-clay ground

cards.decisions: Start as a rare room palette. A full biome needs distinctive rules, enemies, boss and route tests.
cards.existing: Glacial Observatory already uses crystal themes. A recolour is not enough to justify an eighth biome.
cards.idea: A pink mineral room palette with existing crystal interactions; possible future biome direction if its traversal rule is approved.
cards.title: Rose geode cavern direction

cards.decisions: Art-only first; any slippery/water rules require explicit terrain IDs and saved state.
cards.existing: Ice already modifies Dash; do not introduce movement changes merely from palette selection.
cards.idea: Use alternate pale/blue boundaries to distinguish cold channels and their crossing points.
cards.title: Cold channels and pale crossing accents

cards.decisions: Keep large furniture assembled and off mandatory routes; choose collision intentionally.
cards.existing: A camp interaction is a separate proposal. Decorative beds do not heal automatically.
cards.idea: Beds, seats and tables make optional rest rooms readable before opening a menu.
cards.title: Camp and inn furniture

cards.decisions: Avoid introducing durability/crafting systems just because cabinets and tools exist.
cards.existing: This is visual dressing independent of the proposed trader/attunement mechanics.
cards.idea: Add coherent benches, cupboards and tool dressing to Forge or trader rooms.
cards.title: Workshop fixtures and supplies

cards.decisions: Decide wall-attached versus floor prop; keep bookshelves out of ground tiling and preserve LOS semantics.
cards.existing: Archive already exists and shelves need no new combat rules.
cards.idea: Mix full and empty shelves to identify Archive rooms, with small readable story variation.
cards.title: Archive bookshelves and empty shelf states

cards.decisions: Multi-tile placement and wall attachment need approval. No exterior geometry revealed through fog.
cards.existing: These do not make windows shoot-through by appearance. Current LOS/collision remains explicit.
cards.idea: Use narrow window and alcove assemblies for sanctuaries, shrines or crypt dressing.
cards.title: Chapel windows and alcoves

cards.decisions: Do not create false exits or imply projectile blocking from iron bars alone.
cards.existing: Keys and timed gates are already implemented. This is scenery or a skin unless a separate interaction is approved.
cards.idea: A readable optional prison room kit with cells, grates and a distinct barred-gate silhouette.
cards.title: Prison cells, bars and grates

kenney.label: Flag-like counterparts; heraldry needs symbol choices

onebit.label: Flag-like counterparts; heraldry needs symbol choices

cards.decisions: No hidden-enemy reveal through walls. Treat each banner as a prop/assembly, not ground.
cards.existing: The five existing squads are already implemented. Heraldry can improve recognition without a new faction system.

groups.label: Flag-like counterparts; heraldry needs symbol choices

cards.idea: Use banner sets to identify enemy-room themes or an announced squad type before entering.
cards.title: Faction banners and heraldry

cards.decisions: Agree footprint, wall/prop role and whether a variant is decorative. Never infer collision from its sprite.
cards.existing: Solid pillars already exist. This adds art variants; new destructibility is not implied.
cards.idea: More pillar/plinth silhouettes distinguish existing blockers and support structures.
cards.title: Pillars, plinths and architectural supports

cards.decisions: Choose exact existing boon targets after visual approval; leave the accepted Reversal ring intact.
cards.existing: Ring of Reversal already uses Micro #89 / 1-Bit #337. These are art alternatives, not bombs.
cards.idea: Use spare ring silhouettes to clarify existing circular/protective boon identities.
cards.title: Distinct ring artwork for existing boons

cards.decisions: Group by damage/ability meaning; icons do not change damage, range or class rules.
cards.existing: Nine classes already have attacks. No collectible weapon inventory is being added by this artwork vote.
cards.idea: Use remaining blades, bows, axes, staves and shields as clearer action/boon icons and inspected ability art.
cards.title: Weapon and attack icon families

cards.decisions: Every symbol needs a real existing target or a separately approved mechanic. Preserve text fallback.
cards.existing: Current status semantics and 53 boons stay authoritative. Extra bottle colours do not imply new statuses.
cards.idea: Give Burning, wards, healing, currency, charge and boon details clearer consistent symbols.
cards.title: Status, supplies and reward pictograms

cards.decisions: Needs correct corners/insets at two viewport sizes and tiny-size fallback. Card/tablet pictures are not generic frame pieces.
cards.existing: Current menu frames and meters are drawn in code. Text/readability and authoritative HUD values stay unchanged.
cards.idea: Replace selected drawn frame borders with an optional scalable sprite skin, retaining the uncluttered menu layout.
cards.title: Scalable sprite HUD/menu frame skin

cards.decisions: Check glyph metrics, coverage, fallback and text alignment. Keep descriptions and menu actions readable.
cards.existing: No complete lowercase alphabet is established in this sheet. This is not a full font editor.
cards.idea: Use native digits/uppercase glyphs for compact counters and headings, with the existing TTF for unsupported text.
cards.title: Optional digits and uppercase bitmap labels

cards.decisions: Do not leak undiscovered enemies, secrets or exact room contents. Keep 1-Bit cues distinguishable by shape.
cards.existing: Fog/minimap cells are intentionally drawn. Icons must represent known information only.
cards.idea: Use spare stairs, arrows, flags and door motifs to label known room types in the map legend.
cards.title: Map legend and route pictograms

cards.decisions: Cap concurrent cues, respect fog and preserve event timing/RNG. No large opaque effect over a committed attack.
cards.existing: This is static event art, not sprite animation or a particle timeline. Tactical footprints remain dotted outlines.
cards.idea: Assign spare bursts, slashes and small rings to existing hit/block/boon playback events.
cards.title: Static combat impact cue family

cards.decisions: Preserve exact authoritative states and drawn tactical outlines; colour must not be the only distinction.
cards.existing: The mechanisms already exist. A marker does not create a new terrain effect.
cards.idea: Give existing plates, snares, ward fields and timed mechanisms a consistent before/after icon vocabulary.
cards.title: Switch, hazard and trap state markers

cards.decisions: Do not show a mouse/tablet glyph as proof of physical testing. Preserve remapped key text and non-icon fallback.
cards.existing: Keyboard and gamepad already work. This does not add a new input architecture.
cards.idea: Use spare arrows, pointer, keyboard/controller-like marks for concise help while retaining visible key labels.
cards.title: Input and action help pictograms

cards.decisions: Specify all outcomes, costs and save behavior. Card/dice motifs are visual labels; do not infer a card-game system from them.
cards.existing: Three-offer boon chests already exist. An omen must describe a distinct room condition, not conceal another random chest.
cards.idea: An optional oracle shows three pictorial omens describing fixed local challenge/reward alternatives. Pick one; no deck or card combat is introduced.
cards.title: Oracle — visible finite omen choice

cards.decisions: No unreviewed role remapping. A larger pool is not a promise that every figure reads correctly as every enemy.
cards.existing: Mixed has eight shared body pairs; standalone already has distinct current actors. Micro’s character-body rows are fully used.
cards.idea: Use spare complete figures to review repeated enemy/class appearances and selected cosmetic variants before adding more combat roles.
cards.title: Body variants for existing identities

cards.decisions: Doors/archways remain wall/prop pieces; the ochre ground cells are separate. Requires seam/contrast tests and no collision-from-colour.
cards.existing: The mixed choice currently uses Tiny actors and some fixtures, not this complete environment kit.
cards.idea: Review Tiny Dungeon’s remaining ground, brick, stairs and doorway assemblies as one coherent alternative room palette.
cards.title: Compact brick/sand dungeon kit

cards.decisions: Keep readable footprints and explicit collision. Object/multi-tile rail parts must not be ground.
cards.existing: Furniture does not imply new inventory or weapon rules.
cards.idea: Use remaining Tiny props as controlled variants for camps, supply rooms and existing breakable/scenery objects.
cards.title: Tiny furniture, shield and fixture variants

cards.decisions: Do not repeat doors/gates as floors. Identify ground versus wall parts before connected-surface integration.
cards.existing: This would be an optional native palette using existing terrain IDs, not another gameplay pack loader.
cards.idea: A complete 8px environment option could match Micro actors more closely than the current mixed 16px surfaces.
cards.title: Micro-scale walls, passages and surface alternatives

cards.decisions: Respect the excluded flask and ring interpretation. Comment on exact motif readings before binding.
cards.existing: No new full actor body is hiding in the remaining Micro cells.
cards.idea: Review the remaining tiny equipment, foliage and furnishing motifs for existing rooms and UI identities.
cards.title: Micro props, furnishings and remaining accents

cards.decisions: These are assemblies/props; never floor textures. Match open and closed art to the same actual collision state.
cards.existing: Gates and decorative rails already exist. Moving trains/carts remain outside the proposal.
cards.idea: Group remaining cave entrances, doors, closed/open gates and abandoned rail parts into matched sets.
cards.title: Cave portals, gates and rail assemblies

cards.decisions: Approve coherent material families, not random cell mixing. Each candidate still needs its actual ground/wall role checked.
cards.existing: Current connectivity already works; this supplies alternatives rather than missing mechanics.
cards.idea: Keep extra cave wall/ground variants as a material pool for approved biome visual improvements.
cards.title: Remaining cave material variants

cards.decisions: Only tested ground-family pieces may become floor. Reject discontinuities and preserve tile-level collision independently.
cards.existing: Region transitions have many corner variants; they are not new mechanics.
cards.idea: Assemble the remaining dirt, stone and grass patches as coherent ground families for existing room palettes.
cards.title: RPG open-ground transitions and borders

cards.decisions: Parts must be assembled coherently, aligned at the game footprint and kept out of floor sampling.
cards.existing: This is a kit proposal for existing rooms; no new vertical navigation or multi-level physics is implied.
cards.idea: A broad architectural library for improved room entrances, platforms, rails and wall depth.
cards.title: RPG architecture, stairs and support variants

kenney.label: Shared border geometry; colour variants have no 1-Bit equivalent

onebit.label: Shared border geometry; colour variants have no 1-Bit equivalent

cards.decisions: Select complete corners/edges/centres. Preserve uncluttered UI, legibility, scalable borders and tiny-size fallback.
cards.existing: Hundreds of cells are frame pieces and colours, not hundreds of new systems.

groups.label: Shared border geometry; colour variants have no 1-Bit equivalent

cards.idea: Choose a coherent neutral, green, warm or teal skin from the large remaining panel/border families.
cards.title: Alternative colour frame and panel skins

cards.decisions: Approve exact counterparts in comments/preferred cells. Do not equate a doorway, wall or furniture cell with ground.
cards.existing: Standalone loads only this sheet; it must not silently depend on Tiny or RPG images.
cards.idea: Use unallocated wall, doorway, window, ladder and furniture parts as counterparts to approved coloured kits.
cards.title: 1-Bit architectural counterpart pool

cards.decisions: This pool includes ambiguous motifs and variants; choose exact cells with comments rather than blanket-assigning them.
cards.existing: An unused symbol is not a demand for a new mechanic. Every later binding must have a specific semantic target.
cards.idea: Retain spare icons and lettering for future approved boon, UI, item and encounter identities.
cards.title: Remaining 1-Bit item, cue and label library

earlier_decisions.detail: Mushroom scenery was approved; a hittable mist-emitting pod was declined. #315–317 were read as hanging slime, not accepted mushrooms.
Micro #89 and 1-Bit #337–340 were read as rings. #570 was read as a fireplace. Spare barrels do not reverse the rejection.
Abandoned mine-rail scenery was approved. No moving cart mechanic was selected.
Micro #123 was excluded from the flask choice; 1-Bit #740 was excluded from the brazier choice. They remain unused art, not approved replacements.
